headline: HOKA and UGG lift revenue past a milestone; profit dips
summary_short: Deckers posted $1,019.5M of quarterly revenue (+5.7% y/y), its first time above $1B for this quarter, on HOKA (+7.7%) and UGG (+4.9%) growth, but net income fell 6.6% to $130.0M as SG&A growth outpaced gross profit. The company repurchased $338.2M of stock and raised full-year diluted EPS guidance to $7.35-$7.50.
summary_long: Revenue rose 5.7% y/y to $1,019.5M on HOKA (+7.7%) and UGG (+4.9%) strength, partly offset by Other brands' Koolaburra wind-down (-18.1%). Gross margin improved to 56.4% from 55.8%, but SG&A grew faster ($419.9M vs $372.6M), pulling operating income down 6.0% to $155.3M and net income down 6.6% to $130.0M. Diluted EPS still rose to $0.94 as the diluted share count fell 7.4% on buybacks. Cash fell to $1.603B (from $1.720B) after a $338.2M repurchase this quarter. Full-year EPS guidance was raised to $7.35-$7.50 (+$0.05); revenue guidance held at $5.86B-$5.91B.

drivers.explanation: HOKA net sales grew 7.7% and UGG grew 4.9% on global demand; Other brands fell 18.1% on the Koolaburra standalone wind-down; DTC (+13.0%) and international (+8.4%) outgrew wholesale and domestic.
Gross margin expanded to 56.4% from 55.8% y/y; the release does not state a specific driver for the improvement.
Gross profit grew 6.9% to $575.2M but SG&A grew about 12.7% to $419.9M, so expense growth outpaced gross-profit growth and operating income fell 6.0%.
Net income fell in line with the operating income decline; other income was smaller than a year ago, and a lower tax expense only partly offset the drop.
EPS rose despite lower net income because the diluted share count fell 7.4% y/y on buybacks, more than offsetting the income decline.
Cash was used to fund a $338.2M share repurchase (about 3.3M shares at a $103.79 average price) executed this quarter; the company remains debt-free.
Management framed the quarter as a solid start to the fiscal year on HOKA/UGG demand, and raised full-year diluted EPS guidance to $7.35-$7.50 despite higher SG&A pressuring GAAP operating income.
